stage: V3.1 provider-runtime Pilot V2 launcher preflight
symptom: The first detached-launch guard used pgrep -af with a pattern embedded in the current shell command and returned ALREADY_RUNNING although no provider-runtime runner process, run root, or lock existed.
root_cause: The process-detection guard could self-match its invoking shell command rather than an already-running scientific runner.
contamination: NONE; follow-up inspection found zero matching runner processes, no run root, and no exclusive lock.
repair: Do not rely on that self-matching pgrep guard. Require a separate real-process inspection plus run-root/lock check before the single launch. The scientific contract, authorization, pools, arms, runtime, model, and budgets remain unchanged.
reusable_rule: Process guards used to prevent duplicate scientific launches must themselves be tested against self-match; run-root/lock/checkpoint state is stronger evidence than a naive full-command pgrep pattern.
